articles.headline: Week 3 NFL highlights: Best plays, moments, touchdowns, more
articles.description: Sunday of Week 3 will feature 14 games, including an international game in Rio de Janeiro between the Ravens and Cowboys.
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season continued Sunday with 14 games, including nine in the early window, and we'll have the best highlights, touchdowns and moments from all of them.

In the early window, New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn returned to face his former team in the Detroit Lions, and Tennessee Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll is facing off against the team that fired him during the season last year, the New York Giants.

The Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys will take their talents to Rio de Janeiro in one of four games in the second window before the Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams in primetime to cap off the day.

Here are the top plays from Sunday, and be sure to keep checking back once the afternoon games and "Sunday Night Football" kick off.

Week 3 highlights

articles.headline: NFL Week 3: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 3.
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season featured shocking performances in the early window Sunday, including another  turnover-filled afternoon by Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and a three-touchdown performance by Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Commanders backup quarterback Marcus Mariota also led the team to a huge upset over the Seahawks.

Elsewhere during the early window, the Steelers got the best of a shootout versus the Bengals. The Giants defeated the Titans without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, and the Browns won their second straight game.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Jump to:

SEA-WSH | CAR-CLE | CIN-PIT

TEN-NYG | LAC-BUF | HOU-IND

NYJ-DET | NE-JAX | KC-MIA

Catch up on Thursday's game:

ATL-GB

Washington 33, Seattle 31

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Commanders

How did this happen? Turnovers and an efficient offense. The Commanders forced three turnovers, leading to three touchdowns -- two by the offense and another on a pick-six by linebacker Kain Medrano. The offense capitalized on two short fields after a fumble and an interception, while quarterback Marcus Mariota did what was needed. He was smart with the ball, making quick throws and taking checkdowns to keep the chains moving. And he was aggressive when necessary, like on a tight-window throw to WR Trey Burks for his second touchdown. It was an unlikely win without quarterback Jayden Daniels, linebacker Frankie Luvu, tight end Chig Okonkwo, right guard Sam Cosmi and safety Nick Cross.

Trend to watch: Washington did not force any turnovers in its first two games, which continued an ugly trend of only one team having fewer since 2024. But they harped on it all offseason, and the focus paid off Sunday. Can they sustain it? It helped that they played coverage much better than against Dallas in Week 2. But to get more, the front needs to generate more consistent pressure. It'll help when they get blitzing linebacker Frankie Luvu back soon from a groin injury. -- John Keim

Next game: vs. Colts in London (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. (London) p.m. ET)

Seahawks

What was most concerning about Seattle's upset loss? The defending Super Bowl champions came into this game with Sam Darnold back at quarterback, a 12-game winning streak, and as the much healthier team. There were plenty of reasons they lost as 8.5-point favorites, but a big one was their absence of a run game -- something they could have used in the rain. Seattle's tailbacks gained just 39 yards on 17 carries. Rookie Jadarian Price lost his second fumble in as many weeks to set up Washington's first touchdown. articles.headline: Buccaneers WR Jalen McMillan suffers knee injury vs. Vikings
articles.description: Buccaneers wide receiver Jalen McMillan suffered a knee injury in the first quarter against the Vikings and has been ruled out.
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Jalen McMillan suffered a knee injury in the first quarter against the Minnesota Vikings and has been ruled out.

It is the same knee that McMillan injured during training camp that forced him to miss multiple weeks and the season opener. He returned to game action last week in a limited capacity but was expected to play a bigger role this week as the Bucs attempt to climb out of an 0-2 hole for the first time since 2014.

McMillan suffered the injury colliding with Vikings safety Josh Metellus while attempting to catch a pass on a corner route.

It is unclear whether McMillan suffered the injury while pivoting his body or upon contact. He was able to limp off the field under his own power.

articles.headline: Commanders snap Seattle's 12-game winning streak, beat the Seahawks 33-31
articles.description: — Marcus Mariota threw three touchdown passes, and Kain Medrano returned an interception 50 yards for a touchdown to help the Washington Commanders hand Seattle its first loss since November, 33-31 on Sunday.
articles.body:
LANDOVER, Md. -- — Marcus Mariota threw three touchdown passes, and Kain Medrano returned an interception 50 yards for a touchdown to help the Washington Commanders hand Seattle its first loss since November, 33-31 on Sunday.


              The Seahawks (2-1) had won 12 straight, including their postseason run to last season's Super Bowl title, but Mariota was solid in place of the injured Jayden Daniels, and three crucial turnovers enabled Washington (1-2) to win its home opener.


              Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 10 passes for 128 yards and two touchdowns for the Seahawks, and he even completed a short throw on a trick play in the final quarter, but Sam Darnold was intercepted twice in his return from his Week 1 glute injury.


              After Washington had taken a 27-24 lead, Medrano picked off Darnold's pass over the middle and ran it back all the way to put the Commanders two scores ahead with 3:57 to play. However, a penalty during the celebration moved the extra point back 15 yards, and Drew Stevens missed it.


              Darnold immediately found Smith-Njigba for three straight completions, and his 7-yard scoring pass to Cooper Kupp cut the lead to two with 2:51 to go.


              Washington, which was 1 for 11 on third down to that point, converted two on the final drive to run out the clock. Rachaad White caught the Seahawks off guard on a third-and-9 run, going 19 yards around right end. Then Mariota ran for 9 yards on third-and-7 to seal the win.


              Seattle's Jadarian Price fumbled early in the game, giving Washington the ball at the Seattle 21, and then the rookie running back didn't touch the ball again until the second half. The Commanders took advantage of the short field, opening the scoring on Mariota's 6-yard touchdown pass to White.


              Washington nearly took a 14-0 lead, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt's long TD run was called back for an illegal formation penalty. Seattle tied it at 7 in the second quarter on Darnold's 1-yard scoring pass to Smith-Njigba.


              The Commanders went back ahead on an 11-yard touchdown strike from Mariota to Treylon Burks. Then Jason Myers and Stevens traded 57-yard field goals in the final minute of the half.


              Mariota threw a 30-yard touchdown pass to Terry McLaurin to make it 24-10. The Seahawks answered with a 60-yard touchdown drive. On first down from the Washington 13, Darnold found tight end Eric Saubert, who appeared to lose the ball as he neared the goal line, only to regain control of it in the end zone. The touchdown cut the lead in half.


              An 11-yard touchdown pass from Darnold to Smith-Njigba with 11:53 left in the fourth tied it at 24.


              Injuries
              Seahawks: S Nick Emmanwori injured a hamstring in the first half.


              Commanders: LB Leo Chenal was carted off with a neck injury in the second quarter. ... G Lucas Patrick injured an ankle in the first half.

articles.headline: Colts end 9-game skid with 19-17 victory over Texans as Shrader kicks winner with 16 seconds left
articles.description: — Spencer Shrader fought through a groin injury to make four field goals, including a 43-yarder with 16 seconds to go, and the Indianapolis Colts'...
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- — Spencer Shrader fought through a groin injury to make four field goals, including a 43-yarder with 16 seconds to go, and the Indianapolis Colts' beleaguered defense barely held up long enough to close out a 19-17 victory over the Houston Texans on Sunday.


              The Colts (1-2) snapped a nine-game losing streak, the longest active skid in the NFL, and won its first game since Nov. 2 at Berlin. It was the Colts' first victory on American soil since Oct. 26, 2025. 


              Daniel Jones was 24 of 36 for 235 yards and one touchdown, but also fumbled three times and lost two. The second set up Houston's late go-ahead touchdown.


              Jonathan Taylor had 23 carries for 68 yards for Indianapolis. Keenan Allen hauled in six passes for 63 yards and his first TD with the Colts, while Josh Downs caught five passes for 77 yards. 


              Houston is off to its second straight 0-3 start and it was a rugged day for the offense. C.J. Stroud was 16 of 27 for 167 yards with one TD as the Texans finished with just 70 yards on 21 carries and had 223 total yards against a defense that allowed more than 500 yards in each of its first two games. The loss was Houston's first in the last six games of this series. 


              It looked as though Indy's struggles would continue when Jones lost the football and Tommy Togiai recovered at the Texans 46-yard line with 4:40 left in the game. Seven plays later, Woody Marks scored on 1-yard run and the extra point gave Houston a 17-16 lead with 1:48 to go.


              But Jones made the most of his last chance. 


              He hooked up with Laquon Treadwell for 20 yards on Indy's second play. After a 5-yard run by Taylor, Jones connected with Allen for 5 yards, just short of a first down at the Houston 36. Spencer then made the 53-yarder and the Texans' final desperation heave sailed out of bounds short and wide of the end zone.


              Injuries
              Texans: LB Azeez Al-Shaair left in the first half with a groin injury, returned at the start of the second half, left again in the third quarter after re-injuring his groin and returned again late in the game. DE Mario Edwards and WR Xavier Hutchinson both left with injuries late in the fourth quarter. Edwards went to the locker room with a left leg injury.


              Colts:Team officials announced Shrader suffered a groin injury after the opening kickoff, but he didn't appear to be bothered by it. He made all five of his kicks, including a 58-yarder that matched his career long. DE Laiatu Latu left early with a chest injury, but returned in the second half.


              Moving up
              Allen's first catch of the day was not only his first score with the Colts, it also sent him past former Texans star and Hall of Famer Andre Johnson, for 12th on the NFL's career list. He now has 1,068 receptions — two behind Colts receivers coach Reggie Wayne at No. 11.

articles.description: Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.
articles.headlineJa: パルマ、元アーセナル助監督のカルロス・クエスタ氏と契約解除
articles.descriptionJa: パルマはセリエA開幕5試合でわずか1勝にとどまり、日曜日にカルロス・クエスタ監督と解任・退任の道を歩むこととなった。
articles.body:
Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.

The club said Cuesta "has been relieved of his duty" and that "following an internal discussion between the club and coach, it was agreed that the conditions in order to continue this working relationship and the advancement of the sporting project, were not being met. Both parties came to a mutual agreement."

- Goals galore! Why Barça's start to season is best in Europe's top leagues for almost 100 years

- Udinese sign former Real Madrid defender Alaba

- Havertz back at Arsenal for injury treatment

A replacement was not immediately named.

Parma beat Genoa last weekend but only have four points.

Cuesta became the youngest manager in Europe's top five leagues, and the youngest Serie A manager in almost a century, when he was appointed by Parma in June 2025 at the age of 29. He had previously spent five years as assistant to Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

Having decided at a young age that his future lay in coaching rather than playing, Cuesta was given his first chance at Atlético Madrid with their underage teams and after four years there, went travelling Europe to study coaching methods.

It was during this period that Cuesta met Arteta, then part of Pep Guardiola's coaching staff at Manchester City, and after a two-year spell with Juventus' youth academy, Cuesta joined Arsenal in 2020.

He guided Parma to a 13th-place finish last season.

It's the third coaching change in Serie A this season after Paolo Vanoli replaced Fabio Grosso at Fiorentina and Raffaele Palladino replaced Domenico Tedesco at Bologna.

Parma's next match is at Serie A champions Inter Milan on Oct. 10 after the international break.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: LaLiga chief Javier Tebas criticises Man City's alleged rule breaches: 'Equal rules for all'
articles.description: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has said Manchester City legal battle against the Premier League shows why "equal rules for all" are essential.
articles.headlineJa: ラ・リーガのテバス会長、マンCのルール違反疑惑を批判：「すべての人に平等なルールを」
articles.descriptionJa: ラ・リーガのハビエル・テバス会長は、マンチェスター・シティのプレミアリーグに対する法的闘争が、なぜ「すべての人に平等なルール」が不可欠であるかを示していると語った。
articles.body:
LaLiga president Javier Tebas has said Manchester City legal battle against the Premier League shows why "equal rules for all" are essential to protect football's integrity and sustainability.

ESPN reported on Friday that a source has confirmed City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

In a statement, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

The Athletic first reported Friday that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges by an independent panel.

- Ogden: Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

In 2020, Man City succeeded in overturning a two-year European competition ban from UEFA at the Court of Arbitration, after being found to have breached the governing body's Financial Fair Play (FFP) rule.

Tebas had previously spoken out against "so-called financial doping in European football".

In a lengthy post on X, Tebas reflected on those statements he had given during the Soccerex event, which had been held in Manchester during September 2017.

Tebas also called the CAS ruling a "deeply misguided decision" which was "extraordinarily damaging to the credibility of European football's economic control system" and again stressed the same rules must apply to all clubs.

"Economic sustainability is not bureaucracy. Financial control is not a whim," he said.

"And arguing that clubs should compete fundamentally with the resources they are able to generate doesn't mean being against any specific club either. It's about defending a model.

"A model in which sporting success doesn't depend on who has the most powerful financial backing behind them, but on who manages best, generates more resources, builds better teams, and respects the same rules as everyone else.

"Defending this position has cost me a lot of criticism and not a few headaches. But I still think exactly the same as I did in Manchester in 2017.

"There are principles worth defending, even if they come at a cost. And this one, for me, is one of them.

- Man City chairman on club's Premier League charges case: 'Nothing has changed'

"Now, almost nine years after those words at Soccerex, an independent Premier League commission has deemed 114 of the 115 financial breaches charged against Manchester City proven, according to the published reports.

"There's still a way to go. The sanction remains to be known, and the process isn't over. But what's happened once again shows why economic control, transparency, and equal rules for all are essential to protect the integrity and sustainability of football."

"We will keep defending those principles. Just like in 2017."

Information from PA contributed to this story.
